name: youtube-api-scraper
h1: YouTube Scraper via the Official API — Video Details, Search and Stats
metaDescription: YouTube scraper built on the official YouTube Data API v3: video stats, search, channels and comments with your own free key. $0.40 per 1,000 videos.
tagline: Paste video links or IDs and get views, likes, comment counts, duration and tags from the official YouTube Data API v3, under your own free key.
intro: Most YouTube scrapers load youtube.com pages through proxies and break whenever the page layout or bot checks change. This actor takes a different route: it calls the official **YouTube Data API v3** with an API key you create yourself in a free Google Cloud project. Nothing is scraped from youtube.com, and there are no proxies, cookies or logins involved.

The default `videos` mode accepts watch URLs, youtu.be links, Shorts, embed and live links or bare 11-character IDs, and returns one row per video: title, description, channel, published date, duration in seconds, view, like and comment counts, tags, category, default language, thumbnails, live status, made-for-kids flag and topic categories. IDs are batched 50 per API call, so one quota unit covers 50 videos. The same actor also switches to `search`, `channel` or `comments` mode through the `mode` field.

It suits analysts building YouTube dashboards, marketers doing competitor and trend research, and developers who want a stable feed into Sheets, Make, n8n or Zapier. Pricing is $0.40 per 1,000 video rows, and the free quota on one key covers about 500,000 video lookups a day. ActorForge is not affiliated with or endorsed by YouTube or Google.
howItWorks: You paste your own YouTube Data API v3 key into the secret `apiKey` field; Apify stores it encrypted and the actor never logs it or writes it to the output.
Video URLs and IDs are normalised, duplicates are removed, and the IDs are sent to `videos.list` in batches of 50.
Each video comes back as a schema-validated row with stats, duration in seconds and an `isShort` heuristic (3 minutes or less and not live).
Invalid, private, deleted or missing videos become free error rows instead of failing the run.
If your key hits a `403 quotaExceeded` error, the run stops cleanly, keeps the rows already delivered and does not charge for the failed call.

useCases.title: Refresh stats for a video list
useCases.text: Keep a sheet of video IDs, from your own campaigns or a competitor's, and re-run on a schedule to pull current view, like and comment counts. At 50 IDs per quota unit, even large lists use very little of the daily free quota.

useCases.title: Enrich links collected elsewhere
useCases.text: If another tool or a CRM gives you a pile of YouTube links, pass them in as-is. Watch, youtu.be, Shorts, embed and live formats are all accepted, and each comes back with duration, tags, category and topic categories.

useCases.title: One client for every YouTube job
useCases.text: Switch `mode` to `search`, `channel` or `comments` when the task changes, using the same key and the same output conventions. Video rows are always $0.40 per 1,000 whichever mode produced them.

useCases.title: Analytics feeds without page scraping
useCases.text: Because the data comes from the official API, the run does not depend on youtube.com's HTML. That makes it a steadier source for dashboards and automations in Make, n8n or Zapier.

comparisonNote: If you already maintain your own API client, calling the YouTube Data API directly costs nothing beyond your quota and is the better choice. If you cannot or will not create a Google Cloud API key, a no-key scraper is the only option, at the cost of depending on youtube.com's pages.

faq.q: Do I need my own YouTube API key to use this scraper?
faq.a: Yes. There is no built-in or shared key. You create a free YouTube Data API v3 key in the Google Cloud Console in about a minute, with no billing account, and paste it into the `apiKey` field. Without a key the run stops immediately with instructions and nothing is charged.

faq.q: How many YouTube videos can I look up per day on the free quota?
faq.a: Each Google Cloud project gets 10,000 free quota units per day, reset at midnight Pacific Time. Video lookups cost 1 unit per 50 videos, which works out to about 500,000 video rows a day on one key.

faq.q: Can it get YouTube dislike counts or watch time?
faq.a: No. The public API does not return dislike counts (YouTube removed them), watch time, revenue or subscriber lists. Like counts that a creator hides come back as null.

faq.q: How does it know if a video is a YouTube Short?
faq.a: The API does not flag Shorts, so `isShort` is a heuristic: 3 minutes or less and not live. Treat it as a good guess rather than YouTube's own label.

faq.q: What happens when my YouTube API quota runs out mid-run?
faq.a: The actor stops cleanly on a `403 quotaExceeded` error, keeps every row already delivered and does not charge for the failed call. It never retries against an exhausted quota, so you can simply run again after the daily reset.

faq.q: Do I have to delete the YouTube data after some time?
faq.a: YouTube's Developer Policies require stored API data to be refreshed or deleted at least every 30 days. ActorForge keeps no copy after the run, so set a retention period on your datasets or re-run to refresh them.
